title: fix: pause worktree cleanup under btrfs reservation pressure
body:
Related: #202197, #202204

## What Problem This Solves

Deleting a retired worktree can still accumulate large btrfs metadata reservations despite fixed unlink batches. Apparent file sizes and entry counts do not bound outstanding delayed-reference work, and fast commits or low PSI do not establish low reservation pressure.

## User Impact

Retired-tree deletion now pauses when its btrfs filesystem has at least 40 GiB of metadata reservations and resumes below 20 GiB. The existing 128-entry/8-MiB batches and 100-ms pacing remain. Background cleanup may take longer under pressure. Retention, lossless capture, orphan recovery, and symlink protections are unchanged; no configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing host-pressure probe accepts the retired root and binds its btrfs counter once through mount identity and backing-device identity. Hysteresis avoids resuming immediately below the high watermark. Non-Linux, non-btrfs, missing devices and inaccessible counters keep ordinary pacing. This does not add a poller, scan cache, or deletion owner.

The change waits for normal draining rather than forcing shared-filesystem commits. One indivisible unlink and other writers can exceed the watermark, so this is not a hard filesystem reservation cap. Persistent pressure remains subject to the existing 30-minute child timeout and retained-directory recovery.

## Evidence

The real worker regression fails on the pinned baseline: it continues unlinking while reservations remain high. The candidate stops at 41 GiB, continues waiting at 30 GiB, and completes below 20 GiB. Wrong-filesystem and wrong-device cases retain normal pacing. All ten focused worker/pressure tests pass, including entry/byte bounds, symlink preservation, compiled subprocess deletion and absent-directory idempotence. The final focused replay takes 44.93 seconds including cold compiler setup; its six-test worker suite takes 3.30 seconds. An earlier warm worker run takes 1.85 seconds.

Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. All 60 Gateway maintenance/prewarm consumer tests pass (51.69 s including cold setup); the default no-root probe contract remains unchanged. The complete changed check identified strict-return/test-fixture authoring errors, which were corrected, plus the unused CronSchedule export introduced by #202416. This branch incorporates #202551 for that named main-regression gate. All corrected type and lint checks now pass, including every core test type shard. Production and script dead-export scans pass. The full-tree scan still fails on the two pre-existing test helpers described below; the other completed changed-check guards passed. Exact-head [CI run 44771628716](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44771628716) completed successfully: **38 passed, 29 skipped**, head `04ffc48d0b0d3fd58ad6702c98d439c368cd9819`. [ClawSweeper’s final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202563#issuecomment-7044634045) has **zero findings and zero open items**. Automatic GitHub Codex review also has no findings. No CI reruns or administrative exception were used. No production data or live service is used.

### Linux/btrfs and feedback proof

Node 26.12.1, btrfs-progs 6.2, Linux 7.2.12-orbstack; task-owned 64 GiB sparse loop image. Each tree contains 62,000 files / 1,142,784,000 apparent bytes / 63,242 total entries, with one reflink sibling. Five fresh serial A/B pairs follow two A/A controls. n=5 p95 is the maximum, not a production-tail estimate.

| Metric | Baseline median (min–p95) | Candidate median (min–p95) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall, s | 58.014 (53.780–58.572) | 54.032 (53.369–56.573) |
| CPU, s | 3.207 (2.681–3.427) | 3.294 (1.463–3.495) |
| V8 allocated, MB | 215.485 (211.652–228.428) | 219.588 (215.320–224.104) |
| Sampled may_use peak, GiB | 0.748 (0.705–0.766) | 0.759 (0.720–0.775) |

All samples complete deletion. CPU median +2.71%, V8 allocation +1.90%; no material low-pressure regression. Real reservation remains below 1 GiB in both arms, so no real pressure reduction is demonstrated. The apparent wall improvement is influenced by the pre-existing five-second host-pressure brake (494–495 waits), not claimed as throughput improvement. A/A wall 59.049/53.500 s, CPU 3.271/3.107 s, allocation 217.807/209.373 MB; their spread shows this sensitivity. Load averages are retained per sample. Local focused-test compilation overlaps the initial controls/early sample; broad changed checks start only after all timed runs complete. No sample is discarded.

The measured runtime bundle matched after formatting (cmp passed; hashes retained). The final compiler correction changes only implicit undefined returns to explicit undefined returns; no pacing, discovery, or measurement behavior changes. Focused tests are replayed on that final source; the unchanged behavior reuses the measured series. Real-series driver predates the optional fake-counter instrumentation only; tree, sampling and deletion logic are the same. The full final driver is exercised by the following fake-counter trace.

A second private btrfs loop mount binds a task-owned regular file over that mount’s sysfs counter **only inside the disposable container namespace**. The real discovery and pressure paths read it. Synthetic model: 3 MiB reserved per removed entry, drained every 30 seconds of simulated timer time. Full 62k-file baseline peak **112.5 GiB**, candidate peak **40.125 GiB**, both complete. Scheduled waiting **49.4 → 129.4 seconds**, 494 → 510 waits. Physical trace runtime **10.310 → 6.388 seconds** uses accelerated timers and is NOT cleanup-throughput evidence; it ran alongside changed checks. CPU profiles include fixture setup and the accelerated diagnostic, not a production stall profile.

This proves the feedback loop and its wait tradeoff, not a calibrated prediction of btrfs delayed refs. The real loopback fixture does not reproduce the supplied ~100 G incident or measure active SQLite commit stalls. No pressure-driven syncfs calls were added. Both loop images, mounted trees, and fake counter were removed on container exit; no live service was touched.

Production delta: +58/−2, net **+56 lines**. The growth supplies mount/device discovery and the hysteresis state in the existing owner; no policy or state store is duplicated.

### Main regression retained explicitly

The full-tree unused-export scan fails on `installSpawnAttachmentFixture` and `installSpawnThreadBindingFixture` in `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.authority.test-support.ts`. The exact main parent `431392aa4f5b96f5cde7ca32d8583b437d4814d1`, checked out without this patch, reproduces both failures. Commit `c23cb9f0cd39ebf48c8c74a0fd45be9c7eb18d82` / #202522 removed their last callers. This is a main regression requiring repair, not a passing gate or ignored noise. No baseline, ignore, test expectation, or unrelated production code was changed to conceal it.

Final local review: Codex autoreview scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. The rebase to incorporate #202551 is patch-identical by `git range-diff`.
